args.lesson: What worked: a single EXEC did the README-only edit, wrote identical copies to the site and the staging package, checked that the executable hashes were unchanged, checked byte-for-byte reverse restoration and the local link targets, and reran the clean directory and error paths (20/20). The dry run gave digest 5d7354b2... and the review was handed off as SQLITE-LICENSE-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW. What failed earlier: the package README had a blanket MIT label while it shipped third-party CC BY-SA SQL, and the producer checks had not caught it. Next time: whenever a downloadable bundle contains quoted or adapted third-party content, put per-file licensing, attribution, a source link and an adaptation notice in the standalone docs before the first review. This produces no downloads, demand or revenue.
